title: Cap the tax-free pension lump sum
headline: Cap the withdrawals that earn tax-free lump-sum relief at £400,000: Demos, £2bn.
description: A quarter of pension withdrawals can be taken tax-free, up to £1,073,100 of withdrawals, so up to £268,275 escapes income tax. Demos proposes limiting the withdrawals that qualify to £400,000, a tax-free lump sum of at most £100,000, and puts the yield at £2 billion. Only a fifth of pensioners have pots above £400,000, and the relief is worth most to those who would otherwise pay 40% or 45%. Reported as under consideration for this Budget; held flat in cash here.

baselinePolicy.text: Up to 25% of a pension can be taken tax-free, capped at £268,275 (a quarter of £1,073,100).

source.quote: up to £1,073,100 of withdrawals (meaning income tax is not applied to up to £268,275)

alreadyIncludes: The lump sum allowance at £268,275 since April 2024.

terms.label: Demos’s yield from limiting the withdrawals that qualify for lump-sum relief to £400,000

source.quote: if the government limited the amount of withdrawals that benefit from lump sum pension relief from £1,073,100 to £400,000, they would raise £2 billion for the government

rawSource.note: Demos’s figure held flat in cash from the start year; Demos does not give a year or say whether it is static. Nobody in government has costed it.

caveats: A think-tank figure with no stated year and no stated behavioural allowance; the timing of pension withdrawals is easy to move, and a cap announced in advance brings withdrawals forward.

People would take smaller lump sums and larger taxed incomes instead, which spreads the yield over years rather than losing it; savers already over £400,000 would press for protection of rights built up.
Overlaps the two pension-relief cards on this tab, which change the relief on the way in; this one changes it on the way out.

considerations.text: A cap announced for a future date invites savers to take their lump sums first, so the early years can raise little; the OBR would score transitional protection and forestalling.

sources.quote: they would raise £2 billion for the government

considerations.text: People with pension pots above £400,000, a fifth of pensioners on Demos’s figures, and mainly those who would pay 40% or 45% on the withdrawals.

sources.quote: only 20% of pensioners have pensions pots over £400,000
